name: Character Conclave
oneLine: Win the room with memorable conversation, then survive a private popularity vote.
objective: Earn the most votes from other players after everyone exhausts a limited discussion-character budget; self-voting is forbidden.
turnFlow: Players rotate through a public discussion and may spread their character allowance across multiple turns. When every budget reaches zero, each player privately submits one vote; players are ranked by vote count.
actions: I can reconcile the strongest ideas into one clear plan.
aiExperience: Receives the shared transcript and its remaining character budget → reasons about persuasion, distinctiveness, and alliances → emits free-form public text; in the voting phase it converts its judgment into one bracketed player ID.

name: Codenames
oneLine: Two AI teams translate one-word clues into risky guesses on a hidden word map.
objective: Reveal every word belonging to your team before the opponent does, without selecting the assassin.
turnFlow: Each team has a Spymaster and an Operative. A Spymaster gives one word plus a number; its Operative may guess up to that number plus one, stopping on a miss, the limit, or a pass, after which the other team acts.
aiExperience: A Spymaster observes the full secret team/neutral/assassin mapping → searches for a safe semantic bridge → emits `[clue number]`; an Operative sees only revealed labels and the clue → ranks candidate associations and risk → emits one `[word]` at a time or `[pass]`.

name: Liar's Dice
oneLine: Infer a table-wide dice total from one private roll and an escalating chain of bluffs.
objective: Be the last player with dice by making credible higher bids and correctly challenging impossible claims.
turnFlow: Every surviving player privately receives a fresh roll. Turns alternate between a bid that cannot lower quantity or face value and a call; a call reveals all dice, makes the losing bidder or caller lose one die, then starts a new round.
aiExperience: Observes its private dice, every player's remaining dice, and the public current bid → estimates likelihoods and opponents' bluff incentives → emits a higher `[Bid: quantity, face]` or `[Call]`; all rolls become public only when challenged.

name: Market Entry Game
players: 4 (registered default; source does not enforce a range)
oneLine: Talk openly, then secretly decide whether an already crowded market is worth entering.
objective: Finish five rounds with the highest total payoff by entering when no more than two players enter and taking the safe payoff otherwise.
turnFlow: Each round has three simultaneous communication cycles: messages are withheld until every player submits. All players then secretly choose Enter or Stay Out, decisions reveal together, and entrants receive 15 points if capacity is respected or −5 if overcrowded while non-entrants receive 5.
actions: {I think only 2 of us should enter this round}
aiExperience: Observes public batch-revealed messages, past entry choices, and cumulative scores → reasons about congestion, credibility, and mixed strategies → emits `{public message}` during discussion and a hidden `[E]` or `[S]` during decision.

name: Texas Hold'em Poker
oneLine: Navigate hidden cards, public betting, and multi-street uncertainty across a fixed match.
objective: End the configured number of hands with the largest chip stack by winning showdowns or making opponents fold.
turnFlow: Each hand posts blinds and deals two private hole cards. Players bet in turn through pre-flop, flop, turn, and river; remaining hands go to showdown, the button advances, and the match ranks final chip stacks.
aiExperience: Observes private hole cards plus the public board, pot, bets, stacks, positions, and action history → estimates hand equity and opponent ranges → emits one legal bracketed betting action; later streets reveal community cards but never opponents' live hole cards before showdown.

name: Public Goods Game
players: 3 (registered default; source does not enforce a range)
oneLine: Promise cooperation in public, then privately decide how much of your endowment to contribute.
objective: Maximize total payoff across three rounds: keep part of each 20-token endowment while sharing an equal portion of the 1.5× multiplied public pot.
turnFlow: Each round contains three simultaneous communication cycles whose messages reveal only after all submissions. Players then secretly choose a contribution from 0 to 20; contributions reveal together, payoffs are calculated, and cumulative scores update.
actions: {Let me propose we all contribute 15 tokens}
aiExperience: Observes batch-revealed promises, previous contributions, payoffs, and scores → weighs free-riding against reciprocity and reputation → emits `{public message}` in communication and a hidden bracketed integer in the contribution phase.

name: Santorini — Fixed Worker Setup
oneLine: Move, climb, and build in one compact command on a fully visible 5×5 tower board.
objective: Move one of your two workers onto level three, or leave the next player with no legal move.
turnFlow: On each alternating turn, a player moves one adjacent worker no more than one level upward, then builds one level on an adjacent unoccupied square. The fixed setup removes placement decisions; towers cap with level-four domes.
aiExperience: Receives the complete board, its color/worker IDs, and an enumerated valid-move list → searches move-build consequences and blocking tactics → emits one token encoding worker, source, destination, and build square.

name: Scorable Games
oneLine: Negotiate a complete multi-issue deal while every role values the options differently in private.
objective: Reach an accepted deal that clears your private minimum score, while managing veto holders, the required vote threshold, and—in configured roles—a unanimity bonus.
turnFlow: Players rotate through complete proposals and accept/reject votes. A new proposal replaces the current deal and clears votes; a deal passes only after enough acceptances and all configured veto roles approve, otherwise negotiation continues to the round limit.
aiExperience: Receives the public scenario, issues, current deal, votes, and negotiation history plus a private scoring table, threshold, and role instructions → reasons about trade-offs and other parties' latent utilities → emits rationale followed by a complete `[Propose] …`, `[Accept]`, or `[Reject]` action.

name: Secret Mafia
oneLine: Use language, deception, and hidden-role actions to decide who survives each day and night.
objective: The Village wins by eliminating every Mafia member; the Mafia wins when its surviving members equal or outnumber the Village.
turnFlow: Night proceeds through private Mafia targeting, Doctor protection, and Detective investigation when those roles remain alive. Day brings three rounds of public discussion followed by one vote from every survivor; eliminations repeat until a team wins.
actions: Player 2's story changed; explain your vote.
aiExperience: Receives a private role prompt—and Mafia teammate identities when applicable—plus the public transcript and phase-specific legal targets → updates suspicion and deception models → emits free-form day speech or one bracketed target for voting, killing, protection, or investigation.

name: Settlers of Catan
oneLine: Build from an indexed move menu, gather dice-driven resources, and negotiate bilateral trades.
objective: Reach 11 implemented victory points by building settlements, upgrading cities, and expanding roads; the environment omits the robber, development cards, Largest Road, and Largest Army.
turnFlow: Dice roll and resource distribution happen automatically at turn start. A player may take up to ten indexed build, negotiation, or no-op actions; negotiation temporarily alternates with one chosen partner until a trade resolves or either side ends it.
aiExperience: Receives its color, the board, scores, resource information, remaining allowance, and a generated list of viable indexed moves → plans expansion and resource needs → emits `[index]`; if trading, it selects a partner and exchanges structured offers and responses in a sub-dialogue.

name: Multiplayer Snake
oneLine: Choose directions simultaneously, grow on apples, and avoid walls, bodies, and rival heads.
objective: Survive longer than every rival; survival time ranks first, being alive breaks same-turn ties, and apple score provides the next tie-break.
turnFlow: Every living snake submits a hidden direction, then all movement resolves together. Wall, head-on, swap, and body collisions kill; apples grow snakes and increase score, and play ends with one survivor or the turn limit.
aiExperience: Receives the shared grid with every snake and apple → projects all plausible simultaneous movements and collision zones → emits one bracketed direction; submitted moves remain pending until every living player has acted.

name: Surround
oneLine: A simultaneous light-cycle duel where every safe move becomes a permanent deadly trail.
objective: Outlive all other players by staying inside the grid and avoiding trails, occupied heads, and head-on collisions.
turnFlow: Every survivor submits one direction and the environment resolves the batch simultaneously. Each successful move leaves a permanent trail; wall, trail, current-head, and shared-destination collisions eliminate players.
aiExperience: Receives the fully visible grid, heads, and trails → forecasts opponents' reachable cells and future enclosure → emits one bracketed direction; choices reveal only through simultaneous resolution.

name: Taboo
oneLine: Two teams race to decode secret words from clues that cannot use the obvious vocabulary.
objective: Score more target words than the other team across the configured rounds without the Clue Giver saying the target or any listed taboo word.
turnFlow: Each team has one Clue Giver and the remaining members are Guessers. Teams take separate rounds: the Clue Giver sees the private target and forbidden list, supplies free-form clues, and teammates rotate bracketed guesses before play switches teams.
actions: This mammal has tusks and very large ears.
aiExperience: A Clue Giver receives the secret word and taboo list → searches for an indirect but discriminative description → emits unrestricted clue text; a Guesser receives teammate clues without the secret → infers the target and emits `[guess]`.

name: Three-Player GOPS
oneLine: Spend each card exactly once in simultaneous auctions for a shuffled stream of prize cards.
objective: Accumulate the highest prize total after 13 auctions; tied winning bids carry the unresolved prize value into the next round.
turnFlow: A public prize card is revealed and each player secretly commits one unused card from A through K. Bids reveal together; the unique high bidder takes the prize plus any carry pot, while a tie carries everything forward.
aiExperience: Observes the current prize, carry pot, scores, and its remaining hand; because prior bids reveal, rivals' remaining cards are trackable → reasons about card conservation and likely simultaneous bids → emits one bracketed card.

name: Three-Player Iterated Prisoner's Dilemma
oneLine: Talk as a group, then independently cooperate with or defect against each opponent.
objective: Earn the highest cumulative score across five rounds of pairwise Prisoner's Dilemma payoffs.
turnFlow: Each registered round begins with one full free-chat cycle. Every player then submits one cooperate/defect choice for each opponent; all decisions resolve into three pairwise payoff calculations before scores reveal and the next round starts.
actions: I will cooperate with both of you if we keep the agreement.
aiExperience: Observes the public conversation, prior decisions, and cumulative scores → models reciprocity separately for each opponent → emits free-form speech in conversation, then a single text action containing one hidden bracketed choice per opponent.

name: Three-Player Tic-Tac-Toe
oneLine: Three symbols compete to make four in a row on an open 5×5 board.
objective: Be the first player to form a horizontal, vertical, or diagonal line of four of your symbol.
turnFlow: Players A, B, and C alternate selecting one unoccupied numbered cell from 0 through 24. The board and available move list update after every placement; a full board without a four-line is a draw.
aiExperience: Receives the complete board, its symbol, and every currently legal bracketed cell → checks immediate wins, blocks two opponents' threats, and plans forks → emits one `[cell]` action.

name: Win as Much as You Can
oneLine: Coordinate—or betray—across ten hidden X/Y choices whose late rounds carry enormous multipliers.
objective: Finish with the highest individual score after ten rounds by balancing safe all-Y cooperation against profitable but collectively risky X choices.
turnFlow: Rounds 1–4, 6–7, and 9 move directly to simultaneous choice. Rounds 5, 8, and 10 first allow public broadcasts, private whispers, and passing, then resolve hidden X/Y choices together with 3×, 5×, and 10× scoring respectively.
actions: [Broadcast] Let's all choose Y for mutual benefit!
[Whisper to 2] I'll choose Y if you do the same
aiExperience: Observes scores, revealed historical choices, and public talk plus any whispers addressed to it → evaluates trust, alliance signals, and the current multiplier → emits a communication command during talk or a hidden `[Choose X]`/`[Choose Y]` action for simultaneous resolution.
